assessment.summary: ERBB2 (HER2) is one of the most extensively validated oncology drug targets in human medicine, with 14 approved drugs, over 5,000 ChEMBL IC50 entries, 63 PDB structures (best resolution 1.25Å), and nearly 2,500 publications. Both the extracellular domain (targeted by antibodies such as trastuzumab and pertuzumab) and the intracellular kinase domain (targeted by small molecules such as lapatinib and afatinib) are well-characterized binding sites. Druggability confidence is unambiguously high across all dimensions.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 74.0 (66.8% high-confidence fraction) suggests the full-length model including flexible linker and transmembrane regions is partially disordered — but this is expected for a multi-domain receptor and does not affect druggability of the well-resolved kinase and extracellular domains
Only 9 of the 20 best-resolved PDB structures have a ligand bound; additional co-crystal structures for newer covalent or allosteric inhibitor chemotypes could further inform structure-based design
Resistance mechanisms (e.g., ERBB2 mutations, compensatory pathway activation) are known clinical liabilities but are not fully captured in the structural/chemical data presented here
Activity at the transmembrane domain, which mediates dimerisation, remains structurally undercharacterised and represents an untapped binding site
Emerging indications (bladder cancer, colorectal cancer, liver fibrosis) are active areas of investigation but clinical validation data in those settings are still accumulating
